title: Built-in Middleware
description: Learn about commonly used built-in middleware.

data.text: ASP.NET Core includes many built-in middleware for common tasks.

data.title: CORS
CORS for React
data.text: When your React app runs on a different port, you must enable CORS in your API.

terms.definition: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: a mechanism allowing restricted resources on a web page to be requested from another domain.
Middleware that redirects HTTP requests to their HTTPS equivalent.
Middleware that serves static files like HTML, CSS, images, and JavaScript directly.
Middleware that catches exceptions and returns an error response, often redirecting to an error page.

cards.title: UseStaticFiles
cards.description: Serves files directly from disk without hitting a controller.

cards.title: MapControllers / Endpoints
cards.description: Routes requests to controller actions or minimal API handlers.

data.title: Configure CORS for a React Frontend
data.description: Add CORS policy to allow a React app running on http://localhost:5173 to call your API.
steps: Add the CORS service in Program.cs with AddCors
Create a policy named 'AllowReact' that allows the origin http://localhost:5173
Allow any header and any method
Register the middleware with UseCors before MapControllers
data.expectedOutcome: The API accepts cross-origin requests from the React app without browser CORS errors.
